newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softer in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softer in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was softer against the dollar in late trading on Wednesday, with swaps trending further down, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said trading was slow, with the rupiah strengthening to 2,563 in early afternoon before easing slightly on sustained local purchases.
He said calmer regional markets, with traders unwilling to take on new positions at the month-end, helped the rupiah.

Dealers said although the dollar was still in demand, optimism about Thailand's plans to seek assistance from the IMF in rehabilitating its troubled economy continued to underpin the baht and lent support to other currencies as well.
The U.S. bank dealer said the rupiah fell in the late afternoon on London selling, sending it down to a low of 2,588 before it recovered to 2,576/86 at 0845 GMT.
The rupiah opened at 2,565/75 on Wednesday.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,580.25/85.25 and 2,575.25/77.25, respectively.
Dealers said offshore operators appeared to sustain their dollar unloading but were countered by local purchases.
They said local dollar purchases were also supported by a central bank statement that a normal level for the rupiah was between the 2,555 and 2,610 levels.

Paul Soetopo, a director of Bank Indonesia, said after reaching a low of 2,663 rupiah against the dollar on July 21, the currency had in recent days reached a normal level of between 2,555 and 2,610 rupiah.
"Under current conditions, the range is considered normal."
Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the bank sold one billion dollars in the forward market last week to stabilise the rupiah during a recent speculative attack.
Djiwandono said the dollars were sold in the forward market and not in the spot market in order to protect the country's foreign exchange reserves, estimated at $21.08 billion in June.
Dealers said the market continued to stabilise, with swap rates seen easing to approach the pre-turmoil level.
They said dollar liquidity seemed to improve in the afternoon, with overnight dollars falling to seven percent from 13.0 percent, suggesting that further stabilisation was likely.
One Japanese bank dealer said an easing in the short-term dollar market increased arbitrage opportunities for banks with adequate net open positions.
"There is a huge room for arbitrage. Overnight rupiah was at 17.0 percent and the dollar was at seven percent," he said.
Overnight swap was at par/0.05 and tom/next at -0.4/-0.2.
One local bank dealer said the current market make-up spurred operators to arbitrage with the swap market rather than lend long-term with short-term revolving credit.
"If I could liquidate my long-term positions, I could arbitrage now," the dealer said.
Dealers said short-term money remained expensive following central bank tightening, but it was also pressured by the month-end factor, keeping overnight money traded at 14.25 percent.
The central bank had tightened liquidity by raising short-term interest rates and cancelling the SBPU auction to reduce speculative dollar buying.
However, the central bank offering of SBI repos in response to tighteness at month-end helped cool the money market.
Bank Indonesia offered repos on one-week SBIs at 13.75 percent while keeping short-term rates relatively expensive.

The bank offered one-to-two day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, five-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
One-month swap eased to 13.0/14.0 from 13.5/14.0, two to 27.25/30.00 from 28.0/29.0. Three- and six-month swap was at 46.0/49.0 and 98.0/100.0, respectively.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 and the conversion band at 2,559/2,607 on Wednesday.
